message.reasoning:
We have a decision: BUY_OR_AUCTION_DECISION for player p1 (Alpha) landed on KENTUCKY AVENUE, a red property, price 220. Player cash: 460. Opponents: Beta also on same space (Beta also at Kentucky Avenue). Beta's holdings: Indiana Avenue and Illinois Avenue (both red group). So Beta already owns 2 of the 3 red properties (Indiana, Illinois). Kentucky is the third. If Alpha buys Kentucky, then the red group will be split: Beta has 2, Alpha 1. If Alpha doesn't buy, auction will happen, possibly Beta will get it (since they want monopoly). Beta has cash 980, can afford. So buying may prevent Beta from completing monopoly, but also costs 220, leaving Alpha cash 240. Also Alpha currently owns St. James Place (orange) and Tennessee Avenue (orange). So Alpha has 2 of orange group (St James, Tennessee). The third orange is New York Avenue (unowned). So Alpha could aim for orange monopoly later.

Consider strategy: Prevent Beta from getting monopoly on red, which would give them high rent. If Alpha buys Kentucky, Beta cannot have monopoly unless they later get New York (which is also unowned). Actually red group includes Kentucky, Indiana, Illinois. Beta already has Indiana and Illinois. If Alpha buys Kentucky, Beta cannot get monopoly. That is beneficial. However Alpha will have only one red property, not useful for rent. But preventing opponent's monopoly is valuable.

Cash after purchase: 460-220=240. That's low but still okay. Next turns may need cash for rent etc. Opponents: Beta has 980, Gamma 660, Delta 720. They have plenty.

Potential auction: If Alpha declines, auction will start. In auction, any player can bid. Beta likely will win, maybe at low price. Could also be contested by others. But Beta will likely get it. So better to buy to block.

Thus choose buy_property.

Public message: Could be something like "I'll take Kentucky Avenue." Or could be deceptive? Might want to appear friendly. But public message can be simple.

Private thought: Reasoning.

Make tool call buy_property with messages.
